players.product: superconducting QPUs made in its own Fab-1 (84-qubit Ankaa-3 on Amazon Braket, 36-qubit Cepheus-1-36Q chiplet system, 9-qubit Novera on-premises QPU)

quarterly_data.signal: Rigetti Q2 2026 revenue was approximately $5.1 million, up from $1.8 million in Q2 2025, driven by on-premises Novera QPU sales (recognition of previously announced Novera purchase orders); gross margin was approximately 43% versus 31%, varying with contract mix, pricing and the Novera contribution.

Q2 operating expenses were $30.3 million (Q2 2025: $20.4 million), concentrated in R&D (engineering headcount, fabrication, chip design, control electronics) plus refrigeration and infrastructure for higher-qubit systems; operating loss $28.1 million; GAAP net loss $52.6 million; non-GAAP net loss approximately $16 million, or $0.05 per share. Cash equivalents and available-for-sale investments were approximately $541.3 million at June 30, 2026 ($569 million at March 31), with no debt.
quarterly_data.figure: opex $30.3 million; operating loss $28.1 million; GAAP net loss $52.6 million; non-GAAP net loss ~$16 million; cash and investments ~$541.3 million

quarterly_data.signal: Customer C-DAC: Rigetti continued to progress on the $8.4 million C-DAC order for an on-premises 108-qubit system in India, which it still expects to recognize in the fourth quarter of this year after installation and performance acceptance testing. CFO: the Q2 increase in deferred revenue mainly relates to C-DAC prepayments. CEO: the three systems targeted for 2026 delivery (two 9-qubit Novera systems and the 108-qubit C-DAC system) remain on track.
quarterly_data.figure: $8.4 million order; 108-qubit system; revenue expected in the fourth quarter of this year

quarterly_data.signal: Roadmap targets (CEO): drive Cepheus-1-108Q to a median two-qubit gate fidelity of approximately 99.5% later this year while keeping its gate-speed advantage; reach approximately 1,000 qubits, 99.9% two-qubit fidelity and gate speeds below 40 nanoseconds in roughly three years, positioning Rigetti for quantum advantage in roughly three years. An updated technology roadmap is to be published later this year.
quarterly_data.figure: 108Q median two-qubit fidelity ~99.5% target later this year; ~1,000 qubits, 99.9%, below 40 nanoseconds in roughly three years

quarterly_data.signal: Cepheus-1-108Q is built from 12 interconnected 9-qubit chiplets and is available via Rigetti Quantum Cloud Services, Amazon Braket, Microsoft Azure Quantum and qBraid; it operates at a median single-qubit gate fidelity of approximately 99.9%, median two-qubit fidelity of roughly 99.1% and gate speeds around 60 nanoseconds. Coherence times of 25-30 microseconds are now the primary constraint on fidelity; Rigetti aims to roughly double or triple them over the next several years.
quarterly_data.figure: 12 x 9-qubit chiplets; ~99.9% 1Q, ~99.1% 2Q median fidelity; ~60 nanoseconds; coherence 25-30 microseconds

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: at the 9-qubit level Rigetti is at 99.8% two-qubit gate fidelity, and it improved the 36-qubit system to 99.6% median two-qubit fidelity, mostly through design optimization; those learnings are being incorporated into separate 108-qubit systems, not the one serving cloud users. Joint IP with Fermilab (capping niobium contacts with tantalum) and smoother Josephson-junction interfaces are being brought into production chip designs, and adiabatic CZ gates are planned for future systems.

CEO: Rigetti's Fab-1 in Fremont is a 150-millimeter fab and capacity 'is not a concern at all' - a 9-qubit chiplet is roughly 6 millimeter by 6 millimeter, so many fit on one wafer and it can run a number of wafers a day; the limits are capability (150-millimeter equipment, a non-automated line), and Rigetti is looking at options to upgrade the fab for capability, not capacity. He believes future chiplets such as 36-qubit chiplets will take Rigetti to 1,000 qubits and beyond.
quarterly_data.figure: 150-millimeter Fab-1; 9-qubit chiplet roughly 6 millimeter by 6 millimeter

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Q2 capital expenditures went mainly to Fab-1 and additional dilution refrigeration capacity for higher-qubit systems; 2026 capex is expected to be elevated relative to prior years, largely from dilution refrigeration and fab equipment. CEO: Rigetti has begun investing in dilution refrigeration and infrastructure that can support 1,000-qubit systems.

Customer Pittsburgh Supercomputing Center: under an expanded collaboration with HPE and PSC, Rigetti will deliver a full 9-qubit Novera system (QPU, refrigeration and control system) into PSC's new TangleLab testbed, integrated with an HPE-powered supercomputing environment for hybrid quantum-classical workloads; CEO: delivery will be sometime in 2027 (exact quarter not yet known), and the HPE partnership is not exclusive.

CEO: additional demand for Novera QPUs from national labs and universities, with recent wins including the University of Saskatchewan and a research arm of a large Japanese conglomerate; the first two 9-qubit systems delivered this year both went to commercial organizations, and first-half sales growth was primarily driven by commercial organizations buying on-premises systems - something that 'wasn't there at all' a year or two ago.

United Kingdom: under the U.K. government's six-year ProQure initiative Rigetti intends to invest up to $100 million over time in systems, talent and infrastructure; a 36-qubit Rigetti system is currently at the U.K.'s NQCC, and Rigetti is working with the U.K. government on ProQure.
quarterly_data.figure: up to $100 million planned U.K. investment; 36-qubit system at NQCC

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: Rigetti's open modular architecture integrates partner technology - quantum error correction from Riverlane, microwave-to-optical transduction from QphoX (early research), and control systems from Quanta; it buys dilution refrigerators from vendors but designs and builds the overall system. Current systems use coax signaling; flex cables are planned to reach 1,000 qubits, with optical signaling needed beyond that.

CEO: after the change in DARPA QBI leadership Rigetti's plan stays the same, and it remains optimistic it will get into DARPA Phase B 'relatively soon', though exact timing is impossible to predict. CEO: only three gate-based systems above 100 qubits exist (IBM 120, Rigetti 108, Google 105), and superconducting gate speeds of 50-60 nanoseconds are roughly 1,000 to 10,000 times faster than trapped-ion or atom modalities.
quarterly_data.figure: Rigetti 108 qubits vs IBM 120 and Google 105; gate speeds 50-60 nanoseconds
